criteria.text: An unparseable lens (e.g. `a=domain:NOT VALID` or `a=lean:nonsense` or `a` omitted) is echoed back as `a.lens === "all"`, and the response still returns 200 with a non-error body.
For a term that is one of the tracked person's own name words, `terms[].a` and `terms[].b` are both the string `"name"`.
For a term inside side `a`'s top lists but absent from side `b`'s top lists (within the fixture's setup), `terms[].b` is `null`, not `0` and not absent from the JSON.
A GDELT-sourced lens (e.g. `source:gkg`) yields a non-null `tone` on that side for a term with GDELT hits; a non-GDELT-only lens (e.g. `source:rss`) yields `tone: null` for every term.
`a === b` (same normalized lens on both sides) is legal: the response's `a` and `b` term figures are identical for every term.
A person with zero documents in the window returns `about: 0` on both sides and `terms: []`, with status 200.
`src/graph.ts`'s `queries`/`statements` maps gain a `lenses` entry, and `test/graph.test.ts` pins its rendered SQL text the same way it pins `compare`'s.
`pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` pass with the new route, query parser and front-end module in place.

`test/invariants.test.ts`'s import-direction and markup-tag checks pass unchanged with `figures/lenses.ts` added — it imports only `figure.ts`, `api.ts`, `format.ts`, `render.ts`, `docs-card.ts`, never another figure.
`pnpm build` is re-run and `public/bundle.js` is committed alongside the `src/ui` change (`test/bundle-freshness.test.ts`).

`docsText` (across `README.md`/`docs/*.md` as a whole, per `test/docs.ts`) states, as facts and not as a location: that `/api/people/:id/lenses` exists, that a lens is one of a domain, a lean or a source, and that an invalid lens falls back to the full corpus for that side.
`test/docs-drift.test.ts` is unaffected — this issue adds no collector and no default source, so no new criterion is written against it.
